Tanzania are in Uyo to challenge Nigeria for maximum points in their 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying double-header, with a director of the Tanzania Football Federation, Almasi Kasongo, insisting that the Taifa Stars are not intimidated by the Super Eagles’ pedigree. The Tanzanian delegation arrived in Abuja on Sunday but did not reach Uyo until Tuesday morning, delaying the team’s preparations for Friday’s first leg at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium. The Taifa Stars held their first training session in Uyo on Tuesday evening as they stepped up preparations for the encounter. “We are not scared. Football is a game of 90 minutes. We know the quality of Nigeria’s players and their pedigree. We are well prepared and have players from the local scene and abroad who are equal to the task as well. “We are here to fight and get a result. We recognise Nigeria’s quality, but we will go to the stadium to get a result,” Kasongo said. Kagera Sugar and Singida Black Stars have one player apiece. The foreign-based contingent includes Novatus Miroshi of Turkish club Göztepe, Cyprian Kachewele of Ukraine’s Kryvbas and Bernard Kamongo of FC Dallas in the United States. Tanzania have made a slow start to Group L, losing 2-0 to Guinea-Bissau before playing a 1-1 draw with Madagascar in their opening two matches. However, having secured automatic qualification for the 2027 AFCON as co-hosts, the Taifa Stars will use the remaining qualifying fixtures to prepare for the continental tournament.
